title: Masrur the Eunuch and Ibn al-Karibi

keywords: masrur the eunuch and ibn al-karibi
full_text:
Masrur, the chief palace attendant of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, was often charged with finding novel amusements when the Caliph suffered from insomnia and melancholy. One evening, finding the monarch in deep dejection, Masrur remembered Ibn al-Karibi, a famous jester and mimic in Baghdad whose witty impersonations could make a stone statue laugh.

Masrur slipped out to the bazaar, found the jester, and whispered: 'The Commander of the Faithful is melancholic. If you can make him laugh tonight, he will reward you with a hundred gold dinars. But hear my condition: you must swear to give me two-thirds of whatever reward the Caliph bestows upon you, or I will not let you enter the palace gates!'

The jester agreed to the bargain and entered the imperial presence.

Ibn al-Karibi began his performance, mimicking the pompous legal debates of the city judges, the boasting of the camel-drivers, and the flattery of the courtiers with such razor-sharp wit and comical gestures that Harun al-Rashid forgot his sorrow, laughing until his sides ached and his crown slipped!

Delighted by the entertainment, the Caliph smiled and said: 'You have cured my melancholy, jester! In return, ask whatever reward you desire!'

The jester bowed low and said: 'Sire, I ask for only one reward: that you command your guards to administer thirty strokes of the willow wand upon my back!'

The Caliph was astonished: 'Why do you ask for thirty lashes instead of gold?' The jester insisted: 'It is the only reward my heart desires.'

The Caliph, amused by the strange request, ordered the guard to strike lightly. After receiving ten gentle strokes, the jester shouted: 'Hold! The first third of the reward is mine, but the remaining twenty strokes belong to Masrur, who made me swear an oath to give him two-thirds of whatever the Caliph bestowed!'

Harun al-Rashid burst into thunderous laughter, summoned the blushing attendant, and commanded the remaining twenty strokes to be administered to Masrur’s back! The Caliph then rewarded the witty jester with a thousand gold dinars, teaching the greedy attendant that he who bargains for another's reward must be prepared to share the whip.
moral: Greed that tries to exploit another's art gets paid in the exact coin it bargained for.
